newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes higher on export hopes, funds.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes higher on export hopes, funds.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on export hopes and fund buying, traders said.
There was talk Egypt this weekend may buy from 500,000 to one million tonnes of U.S. soft red winter wheat for September and October shipment.
"It had a good push on prospects of Egypt being a buyer later this week," said Dean Witter analyst Jerry Gidel.
Egypt's official commodities buyer Tuesday said he bought 450,000 tonnes of U.S. soft red wheat this week for delivery in August.

"There is an awareness the quality of the soft red winter crop is very good. We have better quality (than last year) and we (U.S. wheat) are very competitive," said Dale Gustafson, analyst for Smith Barney. The U.S. SRW crop last year was plagued with a vomitoxin problem but the crop this year has been virtually disease free.
U.S. exporters early Wednesday said Jordan bought 100,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat for August/September.
Wheat closed 6-1/4 to 11-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with September up seven at $3.56-3/4.

Technicians Tuesday said wheat had turned bullish after building a harvest-time base. Wheat was poised for a post-seasonal harvest rally and the market recently broke a major downtrend line and moving averages had moved up, traders said.
Wednesday represented a continuation of the keen attention to technical buy signals, analysts and traders said.
"Wheat traded above the 50-day moving average of $3.57 in the September but then closed just under it," said Bob Lekberg, analyst with Goldenberg-Hehmeyer. "The fund managers do operate on that."
But the fundamental input of potential large sales of U.S. soft red winter wheat remained a key talking point on the CBOT floor.

"There is ongoing hope that Egypt will be doing more buying after the 450,000 tonnes of SRW wheat they took on Monday," Lekberg said. "They have a tendency to come in and hold these snap weekend tenders."
Smith Barney bought six million bushels of September and bought from three milion to 5.5 million bushels of December, traders said. Cargill Inc sold four million bushels of December, traders said.
In spread trading, Continental Grain did one million bushels of March/December at 9-1/2 to 10 cents, premium March, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 35,000 contracts, above the 32,187 traded Tuesday.

In wheat options, E.D. and F. Man International sold 500 December $3.60 calls at 23 to 25 cents, sold 500 December $3.70 calls at 21-1/2 cents and sold 400 December $4.10 puts at 47 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 12,000 contracts, above the 9,307 traded Tuesday.
